vocab.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: The buildings and equipment a company needs in order to work
The business of selling products directly to the people who use them
The work of stopping products from being stolen or damaged
To have someone as your direct manager
The whole path a product takes, from the factory to the store
To be in charge of a team or a job and check that it goes well
A company that sells goods or services to another company
The work of keeping buildings and machines in good condition

vocab.text: Notice the pair: a supplier is a company, and the supply chain is the road that company's products travel on.

items: A new supplier asks what your company does and what you are responsible for. Answer in three full sentences, not one.
A colleague from the US asks who reports to you and who you report to. Draw the line for them out loud.
Someone at a conference asks what a normal week looks like for you. Say what you usually do, and what you never do.

practice.title: Say each sentence again about ANOTHER person. Watch the -s.
items: We buy from suppliers in Asia.

items.situation: You sit down at a conference lunch table. The person next to you says: "So, what do you do?" You have thirty seconds.
tips: Start with the company and the sector: "I work in retail..."
Then the areas you oversee, not the job title alone.

items.situation: A supplier's sales director asks who makes the final decision on a contract. Explain the line above and below you.
tips: Use report to in both directions.
"I report to... and four managers report to me."

items.situation: Someone assumes you are a lawyer because of your degree. Correct them without sounding defensive.
tips: "I studied law, but I don't practice law."
Say what you do instead, in the present simple.

items.situation: A colleague asks what loss prevention actually means. Explain it to someone outside retail.
tips: Define it in one sentence, then give an example.
"It means we stop products from being stolen or damaged."

items.situation: A new manager asks how often you visit stores and distribution centers. Answer honestly.
tips: Use frequency words: usually, sometimes, twice a month.
"It depends" is not an answer. Give the shape of your week.

answerkey.title: Reveal the model answers
list: He buys from suppliers in Asia.
My colleague reports to the CFO.
Her team works in loss prevention.
answerkey.note: The only change is the -s on the verb. Nothing else in the sentence moves.

listenings.text: Hi Felipe, this is Laura from Northfield Supply. I am the account manager for South America, and I look after retail clients like yours. I report to our commercial director, and two people report to me. I handle contracts, delivery dates and any problem in the supply chain. I do not handle prices, so if you need a quotation, my colleague sends that. Give me a call when you have ten minutes. Thanks.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the retail operations forum. Before the first session, a short note about how the day works. Registration opens at eight and closes at nine thirty. Each speaker talks for twenty minutes and answers questions for ten. We do not record the sessions, so take your own notes. Lunch starts at half past twelve in the main hall, and the networking round begins right after it. Please wear your badge all day. Thank you.

extra_audio.text: First, Laura says her name and the name of her company. Then she explains that she is the account manager for South America. After that, she describes what she handles every day. Next, she says what she does not handle. Finally, she asks Felipe to call her back.
